chunks.arabic_text: كَمَالُ الدِّينِ: الْحَسَنُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ الْأَشْعَرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ يَزِيدَ وَالْبَرْقِيِّ، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ الْبَزَنْطِيِّ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ

translations.en: Kamal al-Din: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris – may Allah be pleased with him – from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn Yazid and al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Hammad, from Ubayd ibn Zurara who said:

chunks.arabic_text: ذَكَرْتُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فَقَالَ: لَا وَاللَّهِ لَا يَشْبَهُنِي وَلَا يَشْبَهُ أَحَدًا مِنْ آبَائِي

translations.en: I mentioned Ismail to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) so he said: No by Allah, he does not resemble me nor any one of my forefathers.

en.summary: In this narration from *Kamal al-Din*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes Ismail ibn Ja'far from the rest of the Ahl al-Bayt by stating he does not resemble him or his forefathers, a comment often interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating Ismail's distinct status or perhaps his earlier death in Mecca, separating him from the line of Imams who remained in Iraq. This highlights the nuanced Shia understanding of lineage and spiritual inheritance, where physical resemblance or name does not automatically confer the same religious authority or characteristics as the primary line of Imams. The remark underscores the importance of distinguishing between the general descendants of the Prophet and the specific, divinely appointed Imams.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about Ismail ibn Ja'far's resemblance to his forefathers?

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ: Ismail, referring to Ismail ibn Ja'far
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.آبَائِي: my forefathers, referring to the Imams' ancestors
